notes: Each eval is a real ticket text run in a local sandbox: a copy of the repo with todo/ rolled back to the commit before that ticket was built. The prompt pre-approves the plan, forbids gh and pushing, and skips the browser check, so the eval measures the build stage: does the loop write tests that actually protect the behaviour the ticket asked for?

evals.name: filters-due-dates-tags
evals.prompt: Ticket #4: Enhance my todo app, I want to add filters only see completed, incomplete and all tasks. I would like to add a due date. I would like to add tags to my ticket and filter the tasks by available tags.
evals.expected_output: todo/ gains status filters, an optional due date with overdue marking, comma-separated tags shown as chips, and a tag filter that combines with the status filter. New tests cover each behaviour and the suite passes.
checklist: All, Incomplete and Completed status filters return the right tasks
A task can be saved with a due date and it is shown
An unfinished task past its due date is marked overdue; one due today is not
Tags are parsed from comma-separated input, trimmed, lowercased and deduplicated
Filtering by a tag returns only tasks carrying it
Tag filter and status filter combine
Tasks saved before this change (no dueDate, no tags) still load
A blank title is still rejected
evals.planted_bug: Change the Completed filter so it returns incomplete tasks instead of completed ones.

evals.name: recurring-tasks
evals.prompt: Ticket #5: Enhance my todo app, I want to create recurring tasks for my todo app. Everything should work on client side.
evals.expected_output: todo/ gains a repeat option (at least daily, weekly, monthly). Ticking a recurring task records it done and creates the next occurrence with the next due date, exactly once. Tests cover the date maths and the one-copy rule, and the suite passes.
checklist: Daily, weekly and monthly next-due-date calculation
Monthly on the 29th to 31st handles shorter months without crashing or skipping
Ticking a recurring task creates the next occurrence with the same title and tags
Unticking and re-ticking never creates a second copy
A way to stop a series, and after stopping, ticking creates no copy
A recurring task with no due date gets a sensible first due date
Non-recurring tasks and tasks saved before this change behave as before
evals.planted_bug: Remove whatever guard prevents a second next-occurrence from being created when a recurring task is unticked and ticked again.

evals.name: search-and-sort
evals.prompt: Ticket #6: Enhance my todo app, I want a search box that filters tasks by title as I type, and a way to sort tasks by due date so the soonest is at the top. Tasks without a due date should go at the bottom when sorting by due date.
evals.expected_output: todo/ gains a search input filtering by case-insensitive title substring and a sort control with a due-date order that puts undated tasks last. Both combine with the existing filters. Tests cover the search and sort rules and the suite still passes, including the existing 74 tests.
checklist: Search matches a case-insensitive substring of the title
An empty search shows every task
Sorting by due date puts the soonest first
Tasks without a due date go last when sorting by due date
Search and sort combine with the status and tag filters
The existing 74 tests still pass unchanged
Search text is not injected as HTML
evals.planted_bug: Make the search match case-sensitively, so 'gym' no longer finds 'Gym'.

assertions.text: At least one file under todo/tests/ was added or modified compared with the base commit
The number of test() / it() cases under todo/tests/ is higher than at the base commit
`npm test` in todo/ exits 0 with zero failures
At least 80% of the eval's checklist items have a test that would fail if that behaviour broke, each cited by test name
After applying the eval's planted bug to the agent's code, `npm test` reports at least one failure
The final comment file names the tests run, their count and result
